_README: dsh-proactive watch list. Copy this file to watch.json next to index.js, then edit the entries below. Every key starting with an underscore is an inert comment: the plugin preserves it when it writes the file back and ignores it when it reads. JSON has no comments, so comments are keys.
_HOW_IT_WORKS: Every intervalMs (default 15000, floor 3000) the plugin reads this file and evaluates each entry that is not already fired. When a condition is met it injects one message into the session with agent.steer(createUserMessage(...)) - the same call dsh-subagent uses to report back to a parent agent - which wakes the agent so it can report to you. Edits take effect on the next tick; no DSH restart.

_TYPES.file-stable: path, rounds (default: the stableRounds config, 3). Fires when the file size is unchanged across that many consecutive checks - the usual way to detect a finished download.
_TYPES.file-exists: path. Fires when the path exists as a FILE. A directory does not count.
_TYPES.file-size: path, bytes. Fires when the file exists and its size is >= bytes. With bytes omitted the test is >= 0, so any existing file matches.
_TYPES.process-exit: process (image name, e.g. curl.exe). Fires when the process is gone. Uses tasklist on Windows; on a platform where the lookup fails it returns nothing and the entry is skipped rather than fired.
_TYPES.port-open: port, host (default 127.0.0.1). Fires when a TCP connection to host:port succeeds.
_TYPES.time: at (an ISO date-time string). Fires when the clock passes it. '2026-01-01T22:00:00' is local time; append Z to mean UTC.

_COMMON_FIELDS.id: Required in practice. Identifies the entry in boot.log and in the default message. Any string, including non-ASCII.
_COMMON_FIELDS.message: The text the agent sees when it is woken. Write it as an instruction to the agent, not as a note to yourself.
_COMMON_FIELDS.sessionId: Optional. Wake only this session. If that session is not open right now the entry is skipped for that tick and stays armed - it is never redirected to a different session. Omit it to wake the most recently active session.
_COMMON_FIELDS.sourceKind: Optional, overrides the plugin default. 'plugin' (default) marks the injected message as plugin-originated, which is not rendered as a user bubble. 'user' renders it as if you had typed it.
_COMMON_FIELDS.form: Optional, only meaningful with sourceKind 'plugin'. Free-form string stamped on the source; 'notice' additionally carries a 'summary' (first 120 characters of message) for UIs that render notices.
_COMMON_FIELDS.repeatSeconds: Optional. Makes the entry repeat instead of firing once. After each fire the condition is re-armed rather than marked fired. Only 'time' (at moves to now + repeatSeconds) and 'file-size' (bytes is raised to the current size + 1) can be re-armed; on any other type it silently degrades to a one-shot entry.
_COMMON_FIELDS.fired: Set to true by the plugin once the entry has fired. A fired entry is ignored. Delete the flag (or the entry) to re-arm it by hand.
_COMMON_FIELDS.retries: Counted by the plugin when a fire attempt fails (no session available, or steer threw). After maxRetries failures the entry is marked fired and abandoned.
_COMMON_FIELDS.firedAt: Timestamp written by the plugin next to fired.
_COMMON_FIELDS.firedCount: Counter written by the plugin when a repeatable entry re-arms itself.
_COMMON_FIELDS.lastFiredAt: Timestamp written by the plugin on each repeat fire.

_NOTE_ON_PATHS: Use your own absolute paths. On Windows a JSON string needs doubled backslashes, so C:\path\to\big.iso is written "C:\\path\\to\\big.iso". Forward slashes work too and need no escaping.

watches.message: The download finished: file size stopped changing. Check the final size, verify the file if a checksum is available, then report the result to the user.
The expected output file now exists. Report what was produced to the user.
The archive reached the 1 GiB threshold. Report progress to the user.
The curl process is gone, so the transfer has ended. Inspect the result and report to the user.
The service is listening on 127.0.0.1:8080. Probe it and report to the user.
The scheduled time has arrived. Report to the user.
Reminder: this entry repeats every 5 minutes until it is removed from watch.json. Report to the user.
The progress log grew past 1 MiB again. Check whether the last answer was cut short, finish it if so, then report to the user. This entry re-arms itself; do not edit it.
